start_here: entities contains graph nodes; filter by type to inspect functions, code, guidelines, CAPEC, or CVE.
relationships links nodes by stable IDs; evidence points to sources and original record locations.
review_issues lists uncertain mappings or conflicting source labels.

relationship_semantics.HAS_REPORTED_WEAKNESS: Source labels the function vulnerable and associates it with CWE-611; not independently verified.
relationship_semantics.OBSERVED_EXAMPLE_OF: MITRE CWE-611 lists this CVE among curated observed examples.
relationship_semantics.RELATED_WEAKNESS: CAPEC explicitly lists CWE-611 as a related weakness.
relationship_semantics.REPORTED_FIX_OF: RESCUE pairs a reported fixed version with a vulnerable version.
relationship_semantics.HAS_CODE: Links a source-specific function occurrence to a deduplicated code artifact.
relationship_semantics.HAS_CODE_SLICE: Links to a source-provided code slice.
relationship_semantics.HAS_API_TOKEN: CWE-level retrieval token, not a per-function call or a claim of unsafe API behavior.
relationship_semantics.CALLS: Per-function, AST-derived call site, with an 'occurrences' count. Not the same as HAS_API_TOKEN.

metadata.name: CWE-611 curated knowledge graph dataset
metadata.scope: All local records tagged CWE-611 in RESCUE and DiverseVul (target=1 only); official CWE-listed CAPEC patterns and observed-example CVEs.

curation_policy.selection: Normalize CWE integer IDs; select all CWE-611 source records; DiverseVul target=0 records excluded entirely (no relevant context).
curation_policy.language: RESCUE labels retained; DiverseVul language auto-mapped per project via the GitHub API (src/language_mapping.py), tagged language_status='auto_mapped_from_github'.
curation_policy.deduplication: Exact code text stored once in CodeArtifact nodes; FunctionVersion source occurrences and labels remain separate.
curation_policy.cve_links: Only official CWE-listed observed-example CVEs are included; no commit-message mention scanning (see module docstring).
curation_policy.functionality: Not annotated in this pass; set by apply_functionality.py.
curation_policy.api_tokens: RESCUE CWE-level tokens retained with frequencies; function-level CALLS edges derived separately via static analysis over every HAS_REPORTED_WEAKNESS function.

review_notes: A shared CWE category is not evidence that two functions are identical or correspond to the same CVE.
RESCUE reported fixes and guidance are source assertions, not independent security guarantees.
API call tokens are source spellings and can include incidental or malformed-looking expressions.
CALLS edges are derived via static AST parsing (tree-sitter), not asserted by either source dataset.

entities.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
entities.summary: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.

entities.vulnerability_cause: The vulnerability in the code is an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability. This is caused by the use of the `XML_PARSE_NOENT` parser option in `xmlCtxtReadMemory`, which processes external entities in the XML data. If an attacker can influence the content of the XML being parsed, they may exploit this to access sensitive local files or execute other malicious actions by injecting external entity definitions. The root cause is the improper configuration of the XML parser, which allows potentially unsafe external entity expansion.

entities.functionality: Scans block devices under /dev for a shared-memory metrics disk whose header matches a known signature and is not marked busy, reads its header and payload using direct I/O while re-verifying consistency after the read, and then parses the retrieved buffer as an XML document with libxml2.

entities.message:
Fix bug #64938: libxml_disable_entity_loader setting is shared between threads

The availability of entity loading is stored in a module global which
previously was only initialized in the GINIT constructor. This had the
effect that disabling the entity loader in one request caused
subsequent requests hitting the same Apache child process to  also have
the loader disabled.

With this change the loader is explicitely enabled in the request init
phase.

entities.message:
feat: XML::Schema and RelaxNG creation accept optional ParseOptions

I'm trying out a new pattern, which is that the parsed object carries
around the ParseOptions it was created with, which should make some
testing a bit easier.

I'm also not implementing the "config block" pattern in use for
Documents, because I think the UX is weird and I'm hoping to change
everything to use kwargs in a 2.0 release, anyway.
